_link.title: I can explain why both excitatory and inhibitory effects are necessary for optimal brain functioning

toLevel2.stem: What does optimal brain functioning require in terms of excitatory and inhibitory effects?
toLevel2.answer: A balance between excitatory and inhibitory effects
distractors: Only excitatory effects with no inhibition at all
Only inhibitory effects with no excitation at all
Neither excitatory nor inhibitory effects present

toLevel2.stem: What can occur if there is insufficient GABA to counterbalance glutamate?
toLevel2.answer: Neurons fire uncontrollably, causing anxiety and seizures
distractors: Neurons stop firing completely, causing total paralysis
Learning and concentration improve beyond normal levels
The brain enters a deep sleep state and cannot wake up

toLevel2.stem: What can occur if there is insufficient glutamate to counterbalance GABA?
toLevel2.answer: Learning difficulties, poor concentration, and mental exhaustion
distractors: Neurons fire uncontrollably, causing seizures and anxiety
Motor movement becomes excessively fast and uncoordinated
The brain produces too many new synaptic connections at once

toLevel2.stem: Which two neurochemicals are used as the primary example of the excitatory-inhibitory balance?
distractors: Dopamine and serotonin
Serotonin and glutamate
GABA and dopamine only

toLevel2.stem: Why is inhibitory neural activity necessary for optimal brain functioning?
distractors: It increases all neural activity levels
It replaces excitatory neurotransmitters
It removes damaged neurons from the brain

toLevel2.stem: Optimal brain functioning requires a balance between excitatory and inhibitory effects.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Inhibitory effects are harmful to the brain because they reduce neural activity.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: Without GABA counterbalancing glutamate, neurons would fire {{blank:1}}, potentially causing anxiety and seizures.

distractors: insufficiently
intermittently

toLevel2.stem: Without glutamate counterbalancing GABA, neurons would be insufficiently activated, causing learning difficulties and poor {{blank:1}}.

distractors: motor control
pain detection

toLevel2.stem: Optimal brain functioning depends on a {{blank:1}} between excitatory and inhibitory effects.

distractors: dominance
reduction

toLevel3.stem: Why is the common assumption that inhibitory effects are negative incorrect?
toLevel3.answer: Inhibition prevents harmful overactivation of neural circuits
distractors: Inhibition has no measurable effect on brain functioning
Inhibition only occurs during sleep and is therefore irrelevant
Inhibition always produces the same outcome as excitation

toLevel3.stem: How does the balance between glutamate and GABA support healthy brain functioning?
toLevel3.answer: Glutamate activates neurons; GABA prevents overactivation
distractors: Both chemicals activate neurons to the same level always
Glutamate inhibits neurons; GABA activates them in response
Neither chemical has any influence on the other's activity

toLevel3.stem: Why would excessive excitatory activity without inhibition lead to seizures?
toLevel3.answer: Neurons fire uncontrollably without inhibition to regulate them
distractors: Seizures are caused by too little neural activity in the brain
Excitatory activity has no connection to seizure occurrence
Inhibitory chemicals cause seizures when they are too active

toLevel3.stem: What would happen to learning if inhibitory activity was excessively dominant?
toLevel3.answer: Learning would be impaired due to insufficient neural activation
distractors: Learning would improve because neurons are more controlled
Learning would be unaffected by changes in inhibitory levels
Learning would speed up because fewer distractions are present

toLevel3.stem: Why are both excitatory and inhibitory effects described as 'necessary' rather than one being more important?
toLevel3.answer: Each prevents the harmful consequences of the other dominating
distractors: Excitatory effects are more important but inhibitory help slightly
Inhibitory effects are more important but excitatory help slightly
Neither effect is actually necessary; the brain adapts regardless

toLevel3.stem: How does the excitatory-inhibitory balance relate to conditions like anxiety?
toLevel3.answer: Excess excitation relative to inhibition can produce anxiety
distractors: Anxiety is caused by too much inhibition and not enough excitation
Anxiety is unrelated to the balance of neural excitation and inhibition
Both excess excitation and excess inhibition produce identical anxiety

toLevel3.stem: Excessive inhibitory activity relative to excitatory activity can impair learning because neurons are insufficiently activated.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Inhibitory effects are not harmful; they are {{blank:1}} because they prevent excessive neural firing that could cause seizures.

distractors: dangerous
irrelevant

toLevel3.stem: Excessive excitatory activity without sufficient {{blank:1}} can lead to uncontrolled neural firing and conditions such as epilepsy.

distractors: excitation
plasticity

toLevel3.stem: Both excitatory and inhibitory effects are necessary because each prevents the {{blank:1}} consequences of the other dominating.

distractors: beneficial
permanent

toLevel4.stem: A patient presents with frequent seizures. A neurologist determines there is an imbalance between glutamate and GABA. Which imbalance is most consistent with seizures?
distractors: Excess GABA relative to glutamate
Equal levels of glutamate and GABA
Absence of both glutamate and GABA

toLevel4.stem: A student with very low glutamate and high GABA activity finds it very difficult to concentrate and form new memories. Which explanation best applies the concept of excitatory-inhibitory balance?
toLevel4.answer: Insufficient excitation impairs the neural activation needed for learning
distractors: Excessive excitation is overwhelming the student's capacity to learn
High GABA causes seizures that prevent the student from concentrating
Low glutamate has no relationship to concentration or memory formation

toLevel4.stem: A medication is designed to increase GABA activity in a patient with anxiety. How does this apply the principle of excitatory-inhibitory balance?
toLevel4.answer: Increasing inhibition reduces the excessive excitation causing anxiety
distractors: Increasing GABA would worsen anxiety by reducing all brain activity
GABA has no influence on anxiety or the excitatory-inhibitory balance
The medication would increase excitation, which directly reduces anxiety

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam asks: 'Is inhibitory neural activity harmful?' Which response would receive full marks?
toLevel4.answer: No; inhibition is necessary to prevent overactivation and maintain balance
distractors: Yes; inhibition reduces neural activity and is therefore always harmful
Yes; only excitatory activity contributes to healthy brain functioning
No; but only because inhibition has no measurable effect on the brain

toLevel4.stem: Oliver reads that a drug increases glutamate activity. Which potential side effect is most consistent with the excitatory-inhibitory balance?
toLevel4.answer: Risk of seizures due to excessive excitation
distractors: Risk of excessive sleepiness and reduced alertness
Risk of learning difficulties from reduced excitation
No side effects because more excitation is always better

toLevel4.stem: Priya notices that both anti-anxiety medications (increasing GABA) and anti-seizure medications (reducing glutamate) aim to restore balance. What principle connects these treatments?
toLevel4.answer: Both restore the excitatory-inhibitory balance from different directions
distractors: Both increase excitatory activity to overcome inhibitory problems
Both eliminate all neural activity to prevent any harmful effects
The treatments work by entirely different unrelated mechanisms

toLevel4.stem: A student argues that taking a supplement to boost glutamate would always improve learning. Which correction applies the excitatory-inhibitory balance?
toLevel4.answer: Excessive glutamate without enough GABA could cause harmful overactivation
distractors: More glutamate always improves learning without any negative effects
Glutamate has no role in learning and supplements would have no effect
Reducing glutamate would be more effective for improving all learning

toLevel4.stem: A patient with frequent seizures likely has an imbalance where {{blank:1}} activity is excessive relative to {{blank:2}} activity.

distractors: inhibitory
modulatory
excitatory
structural

toLevel4.stem: Anti-anxiety medication that increases GABA activity works by restoring the {{blank:1}} between excitation and inhibition.

distractors: dominance
reduction

toLevel4.stem: A student who cannot concentrate due to excessive GABA and insufficient glutamate is experiencing the effects of too much {{blank:1}} and not enough {{blank:2}}.

distractors: excitation
plasticity
inhibition
modulation

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that inhibitory neurotransmitters are harmful because they reduce brain activity. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; inhibition is essential for preventing overactivation
distractors: Correct; any reduction in brain activity is always harmful
Correct; only excitatory neurotransmitters serve a useful function
Incorrect; inhibitory neurotransmitters actually increase brain activity

toLevel5.stem: Dr Chen argues that the brain would function better with only excitatory neurotransmitters. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; without inhibition, neurons would fire uncontrollably
distractors: Correct; more excitation always means better brain performance
Correct; inhibition serves no functional purpose in the brain
Incorrect; the brain already functions with only excitatory chemicals

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that seizures could be treated by simply eliminating all excitatory activity. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Problematic; eliminating excitation would impair learning and concentration
distractors: Effective; removing excitation would completely cure all seizure disorders
Effective; the brain can function normally without any excitatory activity
Problematic; but only because excitatory activity cannot actually be reduced

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that because GABA reduces neural activity, it must cause depression. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; GABA's inhibitory role is necessary and not equivalent to depression
distractors: Correct; all inhibitory chemicals contribute directly to depression always
Correct; reducing neural activity always produces depressive symptoms in people
Incorrect; GABA actually increases neural activity and does not inhibit at all

toLevel5.stem: A researcher claims that the ideal brain state is one where excitatory and inhibitory activity are exactly equal at all times. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; the balance shifts depending on the demands of the situation
distractors: Correct; exact equality is always required for optimal functioning at all times
Incorrect; the brain always needs more excitation than inhibition in every case
Incorrect; the brain always needs more inhibition than excitation in every case

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that anxiety is solely caused by excess glutamate. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; anxiety involves multiple factors beyond one neurochemical
distractors: Correct; glutamate is the only cause of anxiety in all individuals
Incorrect; glutamate has no connection to anxiety symptoms at all
Correct; no other neurochemicals play any role in anxiety at all

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that since both excitatory and inhibitory effects are necessary, any medication that changes this balance must be harmful. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; medications can restore a disrupted balance toward optimal functioning
distractors: Correct; all medications that change the balance are inherently harmful always
Correct; the natural balance should never be altered by any external substance
Incorrect; medications have no ability to change the excitatory-inhibitory balance

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that people with epilepsy have too much GABA. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; epilepsy is associated with excess excitation, not excess inhibition
distractors: Correct; excessive GABA activity is the primary cause of epileptic seizures
Correct; inhibition causes neurons to fire uncontrollably during a seizure
Incorrect; epilepsy is unrelated to the balance of excitation and inhibition

toLevel5.stem: The claim that inhibitory neurotransmitters are harmful is {{blank:1}} because inhibition is {{blank:2}} for preventing overactivation of neural circuits.

distractors: correct
plausible
unnecessary
irrelevant

toLevel5.stem: Eliminating all excitatory activity to treat seizures would be {{blank:1}} because excitation is needed for {{blank:2}} and concentration.

distractors: effective
irrelevant
sleeping
digestion
